source_text: Ἔτι δὲ καὶ πρὸς τὸ πεῖσαι ὑμᾶς ὅτι τῶν γραφῶν οὐδὲν συνήκατε, καὶ ἄλλου ψαλμοῦ τῷ Δαυῒδ ὑπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος εἰρημένου ἀναμνήσομαι, ὃν εἴς Σολομῶνα, τὸν γενόμενον καὶ αὐτὸν βασιλέα ὑμῶν, εἰρῆσθαι λέγετε· εἰς δὲ τὸν Χριστὸν ἡμῶν καὶ αὐτὸς εἴρηται. Ὑμεῖς δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν ὁμωνύμων λέξεων ἑαυτοὺς ἐξαπατᾶτε. Ὅπου γὰρ ὁ νόμος τοῦ κυρίου ἄμωμος εἴρηται . οὐχὶ τὸν μετ᾿ ἐκεῖνον μέλλοντα ἀλλὰ τὸν διὰ Μωσέως ἐξηγεῖσθε, τοῦ θεοῦ βοῶντος καινὸν νόμον [ΙS., II, 3; LI, 4; MICH., IV, 2] καὶ καινὴν διαθήκην [JÉR., XXXI. 34, et IS., LIV, 3; Hébr., VIII, 7-8] διαθήσεσθαι. Καὶ ὅπου λέλεκται· Ὁ θεός, τὸ κρίμα σου τῷ βασιλεῖ δός , ἐπειδὴ βασιλεὺς Σολομὼν γέγονεν, εἰς αὐτὸν τὸν ψαλμὸν εἰρῆσθαί φατε, τῶν λόγων τοῦ ψαλμοῦ διαρρήδην κηρυσσόντων εἰς τὸν αἰώνιον βασιλέα, τουτέστιν εἰς τὸν Χριστόν, εἰρῆσθαι. Ὁ γὰρ Χριστὸς βασιλεὺς καὶ ἱερεὺς καὶ θεὸς καὶ κύριος καὶ ἄγγελος καὶ ἄνθρωπος καὶ ἀρχιστράτηγος καὶ λίθος καὶ παιδίον γεννώμενον καὶ παθητὸς γενόμενος πρῶτον, εἶτα εἰς οὐρανὸν ἀνερχόμενος καὶ πάλιν παραγινόμενος μετὰ δόξης καὶ αἰώνιον τὴν βασιλείαν ἔχων κεκήρυκται, ὡς ἀπὸ πασῶν τῶν γραφῶν ἀποδείκνυμι. Ἵνα δὲ καὶ ὅ εἶπον νοήσητε, τοὺς τοῦ ψαλμοῦ λόγους λέγω. Εἰσὶ δ᾿ οὗτοι· Ὁ θεὸς, τὸ κρίμα σου τῷ βασιλεῖ δὸς καὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην σου τῷ υἱῷ τοῦ βασιλέως, κρίνειν τὸν λαόν σου ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ τοὺς πτωχούς σου ὲν κρίσει. Ἀναλαβέτω τὰ ὄρη εἰρήνην τῷ λαῷ καὶ οἱ βουνοὶ δικαιοσύνην. Κρινεῖ τοὺς πτωχοὺς τοῦ λαοῦ. καὶ σώσει τοὺς υἱοὺς τῶν πενήτων, καὶ ταπεινώσει συκοφάντην· καὶ συμπαραμενεῖ τῷ ἡλίῳ καὶ πρὸ τῆς σελήνης εἰς γενεὰς γενεῶν. Καταβήσεται ὡς ὑετὸς ἐπὶ πόκον καὶ ὡσεὶ σταγὼν ἡ στάζουσα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν. Ἀνατελεῖ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις αὐτοῦ δικαιοσύνη, καὶ πλῆθος εἰρήνης ἕως οὗ ἀνταναιρεθῇ ἡ σελήνη. Καὶ κατακυριεύσει ἀπὸ θαλάσσης ἕως θαλάσσης καὶ ἀπὸ ποταμῶν ἕως περάτων τῆς οἰκουμένης. Ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ προπεσοῦνται Αἰθίοπες, καὶ οἱ ἐχθροὶ αὐτοῦ χοῦν λείξουσι. Βασιλεῖς Θαρσεῖς καὶ νῆσοι δῶρα προσάξουσι., βασιλεῖς Ἀρράβων καὶ Σαββᾶ δῶρα προσάξουσι. καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν αὐτῷ πάντες οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη δουλεύσουσιν αὐτῷ· ὅτι ἐρρύσατο πτωχὸν ἐκ δυνάστου, καὶ πένητα ᾧ οὐχ ὑπῆρχε βοηθός. Φείσεται πτωχοῦ καὶ πένητος, καὶ ψυχὰς πενήτων σώσει· ἐκ τόκου καὶ ἐξ ἀδικίας λυτρώσεται τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν, καὶ ἔντιμον τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν. Καὶ ζήσεται καὶ δοθήσεται αὐτῷ ἐκ τοῦ χρυσίου τῆς Ἀρραβίας, καὶ προσεύξονται διὰ παντὸς περὶ αὐτοῦ· ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν εὐλογήσουσιν αὐτόν. Καὶ ἔσται στήριγμα ἐν τῇ γῇ. ἐπ᾿ ἄκρων τῶν ὀρέων ὑπεραρθήσεται· ὑπὲρ τὸν Λίβανον ὁ καρπὸς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐξανθήσουσιν ἐκ πόλεως ὡσεὶ χόρτος τῆς γῆς. Ἔσται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ εὐλογημένον εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας· πρὸ τοῦ ἡλίου διαμένει τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ. Καὶ ἐνευλογηθήσονται ἐν αὐτῷ πᾶσαι αἱ φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς· πάντα τὰ ἔθνη μακαριοῦσιν αὐτόν. Εὐλογητὸς κύριος, ὁ θεὸς Ἰσραήλ, ὁ ποιῶν θαυμάσια μόνος. καὶ εὐλογημένον τὸ ὄνομα τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα καὶ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦ αἰῶνος· καὶ πληρωθήσεται τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ πᾶσα ἡ γῆ. Γένοιτο, γένοιτο. Καὶ ἐπὶ τέλει τοῦ ψαλμοῦ τούτου, οὗ ἔφην, γέγραπται· Ἐξέλιπον οἱ ὕμνοι Δαυΐδ, υἱοῦ Ἰεσσαί . Καὶ ὅτι μὲν βασιλεὺς ἐγένετο ἐπιφανὴς καὶ μέγας ὁ Σολομὼν, ἐφ᾿ οὗ ὁ οἶκος ὁ ἐν Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἐπικληθεὶς ἀνῳκοδομήθη, ἐπίσταμαι. ὅτι δὲ οὐδὲν τῶν ἐν τῷ ψαλμῷ εἰρημένων συνέβη αὐτῷ, φαίνεται. Οὔτε γὰρ πάντες οἱ βασιλεῖς προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ, οὔτε μέχρι τῶν περάτων τῆς οἰκουμένης ἐβασίλευσεν, οὔτε οἱ ἐχθροὶ αὐτοῦ ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ πεσόντες χοῦν ἔλειξαν. Ἀλλὰ καὶ τολμῶ λέγειν ἃ γέγραπται ἐν ταῖς Βασιλείαις ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ πραχθέντα, ὅτι διὰ γυναῖκα ἐν Σιδῶνι εἰδωλολάτρει · ὅπερ οὐχ ὑπομένουσι πρᾶξαι οἱ ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν διὰ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ σταυρωθέντος ἐπιγνόντες τὸν ποιητὴν τῶν ὅλων θεόν, ἀλλὰ πᾶσαν αἰκίαν καὶ τιμωρίαν μέχρις ἐσχάτου θανάτου ὑπομένουσι περὶ τοῦ μήτε εἰδωλολατρῆσαι μήτε εἰδωλόθυτα φαγεῖν.
pass_a_gloss: And yet also towards persuading you that you have not understood the scriptures, and I will remind you of another psalm spoken by David through the Holy Spirit, which you say was spoken about Solomon, who also became your king, but it was also spoken about our Christ. You deceive yourselves from the homonymous words. Where the law of the Lord is said to be blameless, you do not explain the one who is to come after him, but the one through Moses, God proclaiming a new law and a new covenant. And where it is said: God, give your judgment to the king, since Solomon became king, you say the psalm was spoken about him, but the words of the psalm clearly proclaim about the eternal king, that is, about Christ. For Christ is king and priest and God and Lord and angel and man and general and rock and child born and sufferer become first, then ascending into heaven and coming again with glory and having an eternal kingdom, as I show from all the scriptures. So that you may understand what I said, I will speak the words of the psalm. They are: God, give your judgment to the king and your righteousness to the son of the king, to judge your people with righteousness and your poor with judgment. The mountains will receive peace for the people and the hills righteousness. He will judge the poor of the people and save the sons of the poor, and he will humble the deceitful. He will endure with the sun and before the moon for generations of generations. He will come down like rain upon the mown grass and like a drop that drops upon the earth. Righteousness will arise in his days and an abundance of peace until the moon is taken away. And he will rule from sea to sea and from rivers to the ends of the earth. The Ethiopians will fall before him, and his enemies will lick the dust. The kings of Tarshish and the islands will offer gifts, the kings of the Arabs and Saba will offer gifts. And all the kings of the earth will worship him, and all the nations will serve him, because he rescued the poor from the powerful and the poor who had no helper. He will have mercy on the poor and the needy, and he will save the souls of the poor, he will redeem their souls from usury and from injustice, and his name will be precious before them. And he will live and be given gold of Arabia, and they will pray for him always, they will bless him all day. And he will be a support in the earth, he will be exalted over the tops of the mountains, his fruit will be above Lebanon, and they will flourish out of the city like grass of the earth. His name will be blessed forever, his name endures before the sun. And all the tribes of the earth will be blessed in him, all the nations will praise him. Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, who alone does wonders. And blessed is the name of his glory forever and ever, and the whole earth will be filled with his glory. Let it be, let it be. And at the end of this psalm, which I mentioned, it is written: The hymns of David, the son of Jesse, are ended. And that Solomon became a famous and great king, on whom the house in Jerusalem was called and rebuilt, I know. But it is clear that none of the things said in the psalm happened to him. For not all the kings worshiped him, nor did he reign to the ends of the earth, nor did his enemies fall before him and lick the dust. But I also dare to say what is written in the Kingdoms, that he did idolatry through a woman in Sidon, which those who know the creator God through Jesus Christ, who was crucified, do not tolerate, but they endure all insult and punishment until the last death, concerning not idolizing or eating idol sacrifices.

bible_refs.note: The psalm is quoted extensively in the passage

pass_b_english: I still need to persuade you that you have not understood the Scriptures, so I will remind you of another psalm that David spoke through the Holy Spirit. You claim it was spoken about Solomon, who also became your king, but it was also spoken about our Christ. You deceive yourselves by clinging to words that share the same name. Where the law of the Lord is called blameless, you do not explain it as referring to the one who is to come after him, but to the one given through Moses, even though God proclaims a new law (Isaiah 2:3; 51:4; Micah 4:2) and a new covenant (Jeremiah 31:34; Isaiah 54:3; Hebrews 8:7-8). And where it says, "God, give your judgment to the king," you say the psalm was spoken about Solomon because he became king, yet the words of the psalm clearly proclaim the eternal king—that is, Christ. For Christ is king and priest and God and Lord and angel and man and commander and rock and child born and sufferer first, then ascending into heaven and coming again with glory and possessing an eternal kingdom, as I demonstrate from all the Scriptures. So that you may understand what I said, I will speak the words of the psalm (Psalm 72). They are: "God, give your judgment to the king and your righteousness to the king's son, that he may judge your people with righteousness and your poor with justice. The mountains will bring peace to the people and the hills righteousness. He will judge the poor of the people and save the children of the needy, and he will crush the oppressor. He will endure with the sun and before the moon through all generations. He will come down like rain on the mown grass, like showers that water the earth. In his days righteousness will flourish and peace abound until the moon is no more. He will rule from sea to sea and from the River to the ends of the earth. The nomads of the desert will bow before him, and his enemies will lick the dust. The kings of Tarshish and of the coastlands will bring tribute; the kings of Sheba and Seba will offer gifts. All kings will fall down before him, and all nations will serve him, for he delivers the needy when they call, the poor and those who have no helper. He has pity on the weak and the needy, and saves the lives of the needy. From oppression and violence he redeems their lives, and precious is their blood in his sight. Long may he live! May gold of Sheba be given to him. May prayer be made for him continually, and blessings invoked for him all day long. May there be abundance of grain in the land; may it wave on the tops of the mountains; may its fruit be like Lebanon; and may people blossom in the cities like the grass of the field. May his name endure forever, his fame continue as long as the sun. May all nations be blessed in him; may they call him blessed. Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who alone does wondrous things. Blessed be his glorious name forever; may the whole earth be filled with his glory. Amen and Amen." And at the end of this psalm it is written: "The prayers of David, the son of Jesse, are ended." I know that Solomon became a famous and great king, on whose account the house in Jerusalem was built, but it is clear that none of the things said in the psalm happened to him. For not all kings worshiped him, nor did he reign to the ends of the earth, nor did his enemies fall before him and lick the dust. But I also dare to say what is written in the Book of Kings, that he committed idolatry through a woman in Sidon—something that those who have come to know the Creator God through Jesus Christ, who was crucified, refuse to do. Instead, they endure every insult and punishment even to death rather than commit idolatry or eat food sacrificed to idols.

review.notes: Pass B contains several significant deviations from the Locked Greek and Pass A, including mistranslations and additions. 1. Mistranslation of 'Αἰθίοπες' (Ethiopians) as 'The nomads of the desert'. 2. Mistranslation of 'ἐκ τόκου καὶ ἐξ ἀδικίας' (from usury/offspring and from injustice) as 'From oppression and violence'. 3. Mistranslation of 'ἔντιμον τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν' (his name is precious/honorable before them) as 'precious is their blood in his sight'. 4. Mistranslation of 'Ἐξέλιπον οἱ ὕμνοι Δαυῒδ' (The hymns of David... are ended) as 'The prayers of David... are ended'. 5. Addition of 'May there be abundance of grain in the land' which is not in the Greek (the Greek says 'And he will be a support in the earth'). 6. Addition of 'Amen and Amen' for 'Γένοιτο, γένοιτο'.

Pass B mistranslates 'ἐκ τόκου καὶ ἐξ ἀδικίας' (from usury/offspring and from injustice) as 'From oppression and violence'
Pass B mistranslates 'ἔντιμον τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν' (his name is precious/honorable before them) as 'precious is their blood in his sight'
Pass B mistranslates 'Ἐξέλιπον οἱ ὕμνοι Δαυῒδ' (The hymns of David... are ended) as 'The prayers of David... are ended'
Pass B adds 'May there be abundance of grain in the land' which is not in the Greek 'Ἔσται στήριγμα ἐν τῇ γῇ'
